question:
Balban served as naib to which of the following sultans of Delhi?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Iltutmish
Razia
Nasiruddin Mahmud
Qutb ud-Din Aibak
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nasiruddin Mahmud

Explanation:
Balban served as the naib (deputy ruler) under Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-1266 CE) of the Delhi Sultanate. Nasiruddin was a weak ruler, and Balban effectively controlled the administration. After Nasiruddin's death in 1266, Balban himself became the Sultan of Delhi. He adopted the 'Policy of Blood and Iron' and strengthened the empire by suppressing rebellions and consolidating power.

Extra Facts:
Balban was a prominent ruler of the Slave Dynasty (Mamluk Dynasty). He introduced Persian court customs like 'Sijda' (prostration) and 'Paibos' (kissing the feet) to elevate the Sultan's status. He defended the Sultanate from Mongol invasions and weakened the power of nobles to strengthen central authority.

question_hi:
बलबन ने निम्नलिखित में से दिल्ली के किस सुल्तान के नायब के रूप में कार्य किया?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options_hi: इल्तुतमिश
रज़िया
नासिरुद्दीन महमूद
कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है नासिरुद्दीन महमूद

Explanation:
बलबन ने दिल्ली सल्तनत के सुल्तान नासिरुद्दीन महमूद (1246-1266 ईस्वी) के शासनकाल में 'नायब' (उप-शासक) के रूप में कार्य किया। नासिरुद्दीन महमूद एक कमजोर शासक थे, और बलबन ने वास्तविक शक्ति अपने हाथ में ले ली। बाद में, 1266 ईस्वी में नासिरुद्दीन की मृत्यु के बाद, बलबन स्वयं दिल्ली का सुल्तान बना। उसने 'लौह एवं रक्त' की नीति अपनाई और साम्राज्य को मजबूत किया।

Extra Facts:
बलबन गुलाम वंश (दास वंश) का एक प्रमुख शासक था। उसने 'सिजदा' (झुककर प्रणाम) और 'पाबोस' (पैर चूमना) जैसी प्रथाएँ शुरू कीं, जिन्हें फारसी शाही परंपराओं से लिया गया था। उसने मंगोल आक्रमणों से सल्तनत की रक्षा की और अमीरों की शक्ति को कम करके केंद्रीय शासन को मजबूत बनाया।

question:
Ghiyasuddin Balban (1265-1286 AD), ruler of the Slave dynasty, took up the title of ____________.

[SSC MTS ]
options: Nur-al-Din (light of the faith)
NurMahal (light of the palace)
Zil-i-Ilahi (shadow of God)
JahanPanah (protector of the world)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Zil-i-Ilahi (Shadow of God)

Explanation:
Ghiyasuddin Balban (1265-1286 AD) was a prominent ruler of the Slave Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. He adopted the title 'Zil-i-Ilahi' (Shadow of God), reflecting his theory of absolute monarchy. Balban believed that the king was God's representative on Earth and his authority was divine. He followed Persian political traditions and implemented the Policy of Blood and Iron (strict discipline). He defended the Sultanate against Mongol invasions and introduced Sijda and Paibos (prostration and kissing the Sultan’s feet) as court rituals.

Extra Facts:
Balban weakened the Turkan-i-Chihalgani (Group of Forty Turkic nobles) to consolidate power. He reorganized the Diwan-i-Arz (Military Department) and crushed the Bengal Rebellion. His reign exemplifies centralized authority in the Delhi Sultanate.

question_hi:
गुलाम वंश के शासक गयासुद्दीन बलबन (1265-1286 ई.) ने _________ की उपाधि धारण की।

options_hi: नूर-अल-दीन (विश्वास का प्रकाश)
नूरमहल (महल की रोशनी)

जहाँपनाह (विश्व के रक्षक)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है ज़िल-ए-इलाही (भगवान की छाया)

Explanation:
गयासुद्दीन बलबन (1265-1286 ई.) दिल्ली सल्तनत के गुलाम वंश का एक प्रमुख शासक था। उसने 'ज़िल-ए-इलाही' (भगवान की छाया) की उपाधि धारण की, जो उसके निरंकुश शासन सिद्धांत को दर्शाती थी। बलबन का मानना था कि राजा ईश्वर का प्रतिनिधि होता है और उसकी शक्ति दैवीय है। उसने फारसी राजनीतिक सिद्धांतों को अपनाया और रक्त एवं लौह की नीति (सख्त अनुशासन) लागू की। उसने मंगोल आक्रमणों से सल्तनत की रक्षा की और सिजदा व पाबोस (झुककर प्रणाम करने व पैर चूमने की प्रथा) को शाही प्रोटोकॉल में शामिल किया।

Extra Facts:
बलबन ने तुर्कान-ए-चिहालगानी (40 तुर्क अमीरों का समूह) को कमजोर करके अपनी सत्ता मजबूत की। उसने दीवान-ए-अर्ज (सैन्य विभाग) को पुनर्गठित किया और बंगाल विद्रोह को दबाया। उसका शासनकाल दिल्ली सल्तनत में केंद्रीकृत शक्ति का उदाहरण है।

question:
Balban followed the tradition of ‘Sijda and Pabos’ from which of following traditions?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: Persian
Roman
Mangol
Chinese
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Persian

Explanation:
Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266-1286 CE) adopted practices like 'Sijda' (prostration) and 'Paibos' (kissing the feet), which were inspired by the Persian Empire, where the ruler was considered the 'Shahanshah' (King of Kings). By adopting these practices, Balban emphasized the divinity and supremacy of the Sultan. He strengthened the theory of kingship and enforced strict court discipline. This was part of his 'Blood and Iron' policy to control the nobles and maintain authority.

Extra Facts:
Balban suppressed the Turkish nobles and established a spy system to strengthen the Delhi Sultanate. He fortified border defenses to counter Mongol invasions. His reign marked a turning point in the history of the Delhi Sultanate, where he centralized power. He reformed the Iqta system and strengthened the military organization.

Explanation:
गयासुद्दीन बलबन (1266-1286 ई.) ने 'सिजदा' (झुककर प्रणाम करना) और 'पाबोस' (पैर चूमना) जैसी प्रथाओं को अपनाया। ये प्रथाएँ फारसी साम्राज्य से प्रेरित थीं, जहाँ शासक को 'शहंशाह' (राजाओं का राजा) माना जाता था। बलबन ने इन प्रथाओं को अपनाकर सुल्तान की पवित्रता और अलौकिकता को बढ़ावा दिया। उसने राजत्व के सिद्धांत को मजबूत किया और दरबारी अनुशासन को सख्त बनाया। यह उसकी 'रक्त और लौह' की नीति का हिस्सा था, जिससे वह अमीरों और सामंतों पर नियंत्रण रखता था।

बलबन ने दिल्ली सल्तनत को मजबूत करने के लिए तुर्की अमीरों का दमन किया और स्पाई व्यवस्था लागू की। उसने मंगोल आक्रमणों का मुकाबला करने के लिए सीमा सुरक्षा को मजबूत किया। बलबन का शासनकाल दिल्ली सल्तनत के इतिहास में एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ था, जहाँ उसने केंद्रीकृत शक्ति को बढ़ाया। उसने इक्ता प्रथा में सुधार किया और सैन्य संगठन को मजबूत बनाया।

question:
Who defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the second battle of Tarain in 1192 AD?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Iltutmish
Babur
Alauddin Khilji
Muhammad Ghori
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Muhammad Ghori

Explanation:
In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD), Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan. This battle marked a turning point in Indian history as it laid the foundation for Muslim rule in North India. In the first battle (1191 AD), Prithviraj had defeated Ghori, but in the second battle, Ghori used superior cavalry tactics to secure victory. After this, Ghori left his general Qutb-ud-din Aibak to rule India, who later established the Delhi Sultanate.

Extra Facts:
Muhammad Ghori was originally the ruler of the Ghurid Empire (Afghanistan). He launched multiple invasions into India and made Ghazni his base. After the Battle of Tarain, he captured Ajmer and Delhi. He was assassinated in 1206 AD, after which Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Slave Dynasty.

question:
Prithviraja III defeated an Afghan ruler named______in 1191.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Sultan Mahmud
Muhammad Ibn Abbas
Muhammad Ibn Suri
Sultan Muhammad Ghori
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sultan Muhammad Ghori

Explanation:
Prithviraja III, also known as Prithviraj Chauhan, fought the First Battle of Tarain in 1191, where he defeated Sultan Muhammad Ghori. This battle is significant in Indian history as it marked a major victory of Hindu rulers against Turk-Afghan invasions in North India. However, in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Ghori defeated Prithviraj and captured Delhi and Ajmer, laying the foundation of Muslim rule in India.

Extra Facts:
Prithviraj Chauhan was a renowned Rajput ruler whose valor is described in Prithviraj Raso, composed by Chand Bardai. His capital was Ajmer, and he belonged to the Chauhan dynasty. His defeat led to the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate, which changed the course of medieval Indian history.

Who died while playing chaugan?

Iltutmish

Solution: Correct Answer is Qutubuddin Aibak

Explanation:
Qutubuddin Aibak, the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate, died in 1210 AD while playing 'Chaugan' (Polo). He fell from his horse and succumbed to his injuries. He was also known as 'Lakh Baksh' (giver of lakhs) due to his generosity. He initiated the construction of the Qutub Minar, which was later completed by Iltutmish.

Extra Facts:
Chaugan was an ancient sport, similar to modern-day Polo, popular among medieval Indian rulers and soldiers. Qutubuddin Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate and was the founder of the Slave Dynasty. During his reign, he constructed several mosques and public buildings.

Explanation:
Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq raised the banner of revolt against Nasiruddin Khusrau, the last ruler of the Khilji dynasty, who ascended the throne in 1320 CE. Due to widespread chaos and dissatisfaction during Khusrau's reign, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq rebelled, defeated him, and established the Tughlaq dynasty. This marked a significant turning point in Delhi Sultanate's history, ending the Khilji rule and beginning the Tughlaq era.

Extra Facts:
Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq constructed the Tughlaqabad Fort in Delhi, a major historical landmark. He introduced administrative reforms and strengthened military power during his reign. However, his death remains controversial, with rumors suggesting his son, Muhammad bin Tughlaq, was involved.

question:
The famous Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta came to India during which period?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Chandragupta Morya
British
Mughal
Delhi Sultanate
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Delhi Sultanate

Explanation:
Ibn Battuta was a famous Moroccan traveler who visited India in the 14th century during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-1351 CE), a ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. He documented his experiences in his book 'Rihla', which provides detailed insights into India's social, economic, and political conditions. Ibn Battuta was appointed as the Qazi (judge) of Delhi by Tughlaq but was later exiled on suspicion of treason.

Extra Facts:
Ibn Battuta traveled for nearly 30 years, covering regions in Africa, the Middle East, India, China, and Southeast Asia. His journeys are crucial for understanding cultural and trade relations between Islamic empires. In India, he visited places like Daulatabad, Multan, Lahore, and Bengal.

Extra Facts:
Muhammad Bin Tughlaq introduced several ambitious projects during his reign, such as capital transfer (Delhi to Daulatabad), token currency (copper coins), and the Khurasan expedition. His policies were often well-intentioned but failed due to poor implementation. His rule marked the beginning of the decline of the Tughlaq dynasty.

दीवान-ए-अर्ज दिल्ली सल्तनत के अधीन _____ का एक विभाग था।

सैन्य सेवा
शाही कारखाना
solution_hi:

Explanation:
दिल्ली सल्तनत के अधीन 'दीवान-ए-अर्ज' एक महत्वपूर्ण विभाग था जो सैन्य सेवाओं से संबंधित था। इस विभाग का प्रमुख 'आरिज-ए-मुमालिक' होता था, जो सैनिकों की भर्ती, उनके वेतन, हथियारों और अन्य सैन्य आवश्यकताओं का प्रबंधन करता था। यह विभाग सुल्तान की सेना को संगठित और सुचारू रूप से चलाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता था। खिलजी और तुगलक वंश के दौरान इस विभाग का विशेष महत्व था, क्योंकि उस समय सैन्य शक्ति सल्तनत की सुरक्षा और विस्तार का मुख्य आधार थी।

The author of Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, Yahya Sirhindi claims that the founder of _____ dynasty of Delhi sultanate was a descendant of Prophet Muhammad.

question:
Who defeated Mohammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain fought in the year 1191?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: Prithviraj Chauhan
Yashovarman
Vasudev
Vidyadhar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prithviraj Chauhan

Explanation:
In the First Battle of Tarain (1191), Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori. This battle was fought near the town of Tarain in present-day Haryana (Karnal district). Prithviraj Chauhan belonged to the Chauhan dynasty and his capital was Ajmer. With the support of his ally Jayachandra (ruler of Kannauj), Prithviraj successfully repelled Ghori's forces. However, in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Ghori defeated Prithviraj, marking the beginning of Muslim rule in North India.

Extra Facts:
Muhammad Ghori ascended the throne of Ghazni in 1173 CE and launched invasions into India, capturing Multan, Sindh, and Punjab. Prithviraj Chauhan, also known as 'Rai Pithora', was a skilled warrior and poet. His court poet Chand Bardai composed the famous epic 'Prithviraj Raso'.

विद्याधर
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पृथ्वीराज चौहान

Explanation:
1191 ईस्वी में लड़े गए तराइन के प्रथम युद्ध में पृथ्वीराज चौहान ने मोहम्मद गोरी को हराया था। यह युद्ध वर्तमान हरियाणा के करनाल जिले के निकट तराइन नामक स्थान पर लड़ा गया था। पृथ्वीराज चौहान, चौहान वंश के शासक थे और उनकी राजधानी अजमेर थी। इस युद्ध में पृथ्वीराज चौहान ने अपने सहयोगी राजा जयचंद (कन्नौज के शासक) की मदद से गोरी की सेना को पराजित किया। हालांकि, 1192 ईस्वी में लड़े गए तराइन के द्वितीय युद्ध में गोरी ने पृथ्वीराज को हराकर उत्तर भारत में मुस्लिम शासन की नींव रखी।

Extra Facts:

question:
‘Amir-al- Khayl’ is an Arabic title that is usually translated ‘Commander of the Faithful’ or ‘Leader of the Faithful’. Who among the following was given this designation?

Naseeruddin Mohd
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jamal-ud-Din Yaqut

Explanation:
The title 'Amir-al-Khayl' (Commander of the Faithful or Leader of the Horsemen) was given to Jamal-ud-Din Yaqut, an African (Abyssinian) noble during the reign of Razia Sultana (1236-1240 CE) of the Delhi Sultanate. He was a close confidant of Razia and was appointed as the superintendent of the royal stables. His growing influence angered the Turkish nobility, leading to a rebellion that ultimately resulted in Razia's downfall.

Extra Facts:
Razia Sultana was the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. She defied gender norms by ruling without a veil. The rebellion against her was led by Malik Ikhtiar-ud-din Altunia, a former governor, who killed Yaqut and later married Razia in a political alliance.

question_hi:
'अमीर-अल-खयल' एक अरबी उपाधि है जिसका अनुवाद आमतौर पर 'वफादार का कमांडर' या 'वफादारो का नेता' किया जाता है। निम्नलिखित में से किसे यह उपाधि दी गयी थी?

solution_hi:

Explanation:
'अमीर-अल-खयल' एक अरबी उपाधि थी जिसका अर्थ है 'वफादारों का नेता' या 'घुड़सवारों का कमांडर'। यह उपाधि जमाल-उद-दीन याकूत को दी गई थी, जो दिल्ली सल्तनत के समय में रजिया सुल्तान के शासनकाल (1236-1240 ई.) में एक प्रमुख अफ्रीकी (हब्शी) सरदार थे। वह रजिया सुल्तान के करीबी सलाहकारों में से एक थे और उन्हें घुड़सवार सेना का प्रमुख नियुक्त किया गया था। उनकी निकटता और प्रभाव के कारण तुर्की अमीरों ने उनके खिलाफ विद्रोह कर दिया, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप रजिया सुल्तान का पतन हुआ।

question:
In which year was the Battle of Peshawar fought between Raja Jayapal and Mahmud Ghazni?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: 1001
1112
1305
1258
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1001

Explanation:
The Battle of Peshawar was fought in 1001 CE between Raja Jayapala (ruler of the Hindu Shahi dynasty) and Mahmud of Ghazni. This battle marked the beginning of Mahmud Ghazni's invasions into India. Jayapala faced defeat and later committed self-immolation. The battle is significant in Indian history as it paved the way for Turk-Afghan invasions in northwestern India.

Extra Facts:
Mahmud Ghazni launched 17 invasions into India, with the destruction of the Somnath Temple (1025 CE) being the most infamous. The Hindu Shahi dynasty ruled the Kabul and Punjab regions for nearly 200 years. After Jayapala, his son Anandapala and grandson Trilochanapala continued resisting Ghazni.

question:

question:
Which of the following systems of the Delhi sultanate had a influence on the Bahmani and Vijayanagar kingdoms?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Walis
Chahalgani
Bitikchi
Iqtadari
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Iqtadari

Explanation:
The Iqtadari system of the Delhi Sultanate significantly influenced the Bahmani and Vijayanagar kingdoms. This system was related to land administration and revenue collection, where military officers and officials were granted rights to collect taxes. The Bahmani Kingdom adopted it as 'Jagirdari', while Vijayanagar developed the 'Amara' system. This arrangement helped strengthen military and administrative control.

Extra Facts:
The Iqtadari system was introduced by Muhammad Ghori and Iltutmish. In the Bahmani Kingdom, it evolved into 'Taraf' and 'Sarkar'. Vijayanagar’s 'Nayankara system' was also influenced by it, where land grants were given to warriors.

question:
Who among the following ended the Kakatiya dynasty rule?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Cholas
Delhi Sultanate
Chalukyas
Guptas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Delhi Sultanate

Explanation:
The Kakatiya dynasty ruled from 1083 to 1323 CE in South India (present-day Telangana and Andhra Pradesh). The dynasty was ended by the Delhi Sultanate under the command of Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's generals, Malik Kafur and later Ulugh Khan (Muhammad bin Tughlaq). In 1323 CE, the Warangal Fort was attacked, and the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra Deva was defeated and captured, leading to the fall of the Kakatiya dynasty.

Extra Facts:
The Kakatiya dynasty produced notable rulers like Rudrama Devi, one of India's earliest female monarchs, who promoted art, literature, and architecture. The Kakatiyas built iconic monuments such as the Ramappa Temple (Warangal) and the Thousand Pillar Temple, which are now UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

question:
The office of Diwan-i-Insha dealt with which affair in administration?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Military
Religious affairs
Finance
State correspondence
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State correspondence

Explanation:
The Diwan-i-Insha was an important office in the Mughal administration that dealt with state correspondence. This department was responsible for drafting royal decrees (firmans), letters, proclamations, and other official documents, as well as maintaining their records. The head of this office was called the Dabir-i-Khas, who was skilled in calligraphy and precise language to ensure the accuracy and elegance of royal communications. This system was a crucial part of the Mughal Empire's centralized administrative structure, ensuring effective communication across the vast empire.

Extra Facts:
The Mughal administration had several other diwans, such as Diwan-i-Arz (military affairs), Diwan-i-Wazarat (finance), and Diwan-i-Risalat (religious affairs). The Diwan-i-Insha was particularly known for preparing documents in Persian, the official language of the Mughal court. This office played a key role in maintaining transparency and order in the empire.

Balban’s rule as an absolute despot led to which of the following events?

Destruction of the Forty
solution:

Explanation:
Balban (1266-1286 CE) was a powerful ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who adopted an autocratic style of governance. To consolidate his authority, he destroyed 'The Forty' (Chalisa), a group of forty Turkic nobles who challenged the Sultan's power. Balban followed the policy of 'Blood and Iron' and proclaimed himself as 'Zill-e-Ilahi' (Shadow of God) in the Persian tradition. He also restricted the practice of granting Jagirs to nobles to reduce their influence.

Extra Facts:
Balban introduced Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the Sultan's feet) to enhance royal dignity. He defended the Sultanate against Mongol invasions and crushed the rebellion of Tughril Khan, the governor of Bengal. His reign is noted for military and administrative reforms.

question:
Who was the Sultan of Delhi at the time of the establishment of Vijayanagara Empire?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Nasiruddin Mahmud
Iltutmish
Mohammad bin Tughlaq
Alauddin Khilji
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mohammad bin Tughlaq

Explanation:
The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 CE by Harihara and Bukka. At that time, Mohammad bin Tughlaq (1325-1351 CE) was the Sultan of Delhi. He was the second ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty and was infamous for his eccentric decisions, such as shifting the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad. The Vijayanagara Empire was founded to counter the influence of the Delhi Sultanate in South India.

Extra Facts:
The Vijayanagara Empire was a major Hindu kingdom in South India that ruled for nearly 300 years. Its capital was Hampi, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Krishnadevaraya (1509-1529) was its greatest ruler, known for constructing the Rayagopuram and Vittala Temple.

He introduced practices like Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the feet) to elevate the Sultan’s prestige. He appointed kinsmen (The Forty) to key positions and bolstered military power.

Balban reorganized the Diwan-i-Arz (Military Department) and fortified frontier regions. He crushed rebellions in Bengal and Mewat and established a spy network to counter Mongol threats. His reign is considered the golden era of centralization and discipline in the Delhi Sultanate.

निम्नलिखित में से किसने विद्रोहियों का सफाया कर विस्तार के स्थान पर समेकन (consolidation) की नीति अपनाई?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: शमसुद्दीन इल्तुतमिश
रजिया
नसीरुद्दीन महमूद
गयासुद्दीन बलबन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है गयासुद्दीन बलबन

Explanation:
गयासुद्दीन बलबन (1266-1286 ई.) ने दिल्ली सल्तनत के दौरान विस्तार के बजाय समेकन (consolidation) की नीति अपनाई। उसने मंगोलों के आक्रमण और आंतरिक विद्रोहों से निपटने के लिए एक मजबूत केंद्रीय सत्ता स्थापित की। बलबन ने 'लौह और रक्त' की नीति अपनाकर विद्रोहियों का सफाया किया और साम्राज्य को सुदृढ़ बनाया। उसने सिजदा (झुककर प्रणाम) और पाबोस (पैर चूमना) जैसी प्रथाएँ शुरू कीं ताकि सुल्तान की प्रतिष्ठा बढ़े। उसने रक्त संबंधियों (फॉर्टी) को महत्वपूर्ण पद दिए और सैन्य शक्ति को मजबूत किया।

Extra Facts:
बलबन ने दीवान-ए-अर्ज (सैन्य विभाग) को पुनर्गठित किया और सीमा क्षेत्रों में मजबूत गढ़ बनाए। उसने बंगाल और मेवात के विद्रोहों को कुचला और मंगोलों के खतरे को रोकने के लिए निगरानी प्रणाली विकसित की। उसका शासनकाल दिल्ली सल्तनत में केंद्रीकरण और अनुशासन का स्वर्ण युग माना जाता है।

question:
With reference to the administration of Delhi Sultanate, which of the following was the department of State Correspondence?

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: Diwan-i-arz
Diwan-i-khairat
Diwan-i -risalat
Diwan-i-insha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Diwan-i-insha

Explanation:
In the administration of the Delhi Sultanate, 'Diwan-i-insha' was the department of State Correspondence. This department managed the official letters, proclamations, royal decrees (farmans), and diplomatic correspondence of the Sultan. Its head was called 'Dabir-i-Khas', who was responsible for drafting documents in Arabic and Persian. This department played a crucial role in maintaining administrative efficiency. Among the other options, 'Diwan-i-arz' was the military department, 'Diwan-i-khairat' dealt with charity and religious endowments, while 'Diwan-i-risalat' handled religious affairs.

Extra Facts:
The Delhi Sultanate had a centralized administrative system managed through various 'diwans'. 'Diwan-i-wazarat' was the finance department headed by the Wazir. 'Diwan-i-qaza' dealt with judicial matters. Sultans like Iltutmish and Balban strengthened this system.

question_hi:
दिल्ली सल्तनत के प्रशासन के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन राज्य पत्राचार विभाग था?

[SSC CGL 2021]
options_hi: दीवान-ए-अर्जी
दीवान-ए-खैरत
दीवान-ए-रिसालत
दीवान-ए-इंशा
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है दीवान-ए-इंशा

Explanation:
दिल्ली सल्तनत के प्रशासन में 'दीवान-ए-इंशा' राज्य पत्राचार विभाग था। यह विभाग सुल्तान के आधिकारिक पत्रों, घोषणाओं, फरमानों और राजनयिक पत्राचार का प्रबंधन करता था। इसका प्रमुख 'दबीर-ए-खास' कहलाता था, जो अरबी और फारसी भाषा में पत्राचार करता था। यह विभाग सल्तनत काल में प्रशासनिक दक्षता बनाए रखने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण था। अन्य विकल्पों में, 'दीवान-ए-अर्जी' सैन्य विभाग था, 'दीवान-ए-खैरत' दान और धर्मार्थ कार्यों से संबंधित था, जबकि 'दीवान-ए-रिसालत' धार्मिक मामलों का प्रभारी था।

Extra Facts:
दिल्ली सल्तनत में प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था केंद्रीकृत थी और विभिन्न दीवानों के माध्यम से संचालित होती थी। 'दीवान-ए-वजारत' वित्त विभाग था, जिसका प्रमुख वजीर होता था। 'दीवान-ए-क़ज़ा' न्यायिक मामलों का प्रभारी था। सुल्तान इल्तुतमिश ने प्रशासनिक सुधार किए और बलबन ने इसे और मजबूत किया।
